title: Insufficient Cryptographic PRNG Seeding
pattern: Initializing a pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) meant for cryptographic key or token creation with low-entropy parameters, such as the current process identifier or a low-resolution system timestamp.
why_bad: PIDs and boot timestamps are highly predictable or trivially brute-forced. If the PRNG seed space is small (e.g. only 32,768 possible seeds), an attacker can generate all possible key combinations in seconds, completely breaking encryption.
detection: PRNG seeding functions taking process IDs, sequential thread counters, or low-resolution timestamps as inputs without cryptographic entropy sources.
fix: Always seed cryptographic PRNGs with high-entropy source values retrieved directly from OS-level entropy interfaces (like `/dev/urandom` or system cryptocalls).
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 1, p. 31; Ch 2, p. 31.
